strengths: Backward integration — in-house design, contracting and facade manufacturing — keeps gross margin at 44–45% (Moody's: 'strong backward integration')
Revenue backlog of AED 17.3 bn to be recognised over one to three years; more than 80% of 2026 deliveries already sold
Front-loaded payment plans (about 70% collected during construction) and the RERA escrow regime fund construction without the balance sheet
Market access proven: four USD 500m sukuk in twelve months, each four to five times covered, half the demand international
Equity has tripled to AED 9.75 bn through retained earnings; no dividends are permitted under the sukuk
concerns: Only AED 0.39 bn of the AED 10.6 bn reported cash sits outside escrow, against AED 3.56 bn of debt due within twelve months and the USD 500m sukuk in February 2027 — Moody's: liquidity 'weaker than anticipated'
Growth is debt-funded and fast: gross debt AED 3.3 bn (Dec 2024) → 8.3 bn (Dec 2025) → 11.5 bn (Jun 2026), while unit sales fell 5% in H1 2026

AED 1.23 bn is owed to the company by its shareholder and key managers for land and units sold to them, unpaid; fair-value gains on units contributed to related funds flow through EBITDA — governance is the recurring agency criticism (100% family owned, Fitch ESG governance score 4)
Secondary prices of 84–89 on the 2029–2031 sukuk mean any refinancing would cost 12–13%, far above the 7.75–8.4% coupons
Branded ultra-luxury towers (Bugatti, Jacob & Co, Mercedes-Benz Places) are absent from the 2026 handover schedule; Moody's: 'limited execution track record in uber luxury'
36% of debt is secured on land with shareholder guarantees, structurally ahead of the sukuk; there is no committed revolving facility

Reporting quality of the headline sales figure: it appears in no financial statement, has no published definition (cancellations, VAT, registration fees, related-party and fund purchases all unstated), does not reconcile to its own quarters in FY2025, and was restated once without explanation. The audited IFRS 15 backlog note is the sounder measure of the same activity.

view.capacity: On paper the business earns its interest many times over and leverage on an EBITDA basis is under two times. The problem is the shape of the cash, not the size of the profit. Almost everything the company calls cash is customer money in RERA escrow, released only as inspectors certify progress. Free cash outside escrow was AED 393 million at the end of June against AED 3.6 billion of debt falling due within a year, and the half-year burned roughly AED 1.5 billion buying land. The February 2027 sukuk (AED 1.84 billion) is therefore payable only if the ten mainstream towers scheduled for the second half of 2026 (AED 7.5 billion of value, 94% sold, about 80% collected) hand over on time and release their escrow, or if the market reopens for a refinancing. The company says AED 1.8 billion has already come in from three handovers since June.
view.refinancing: The market is charging 12–13% to hold the 2029–2031 paper and the 2027 sukuk yields 10–13%. A new issue at those levels would be expensive but is not impossible for a company that placed USD 2 billion in the year to February; a bank bridge secured on the new Nad Al Sheba land is the more likely route if handovers slip. A downgrade to B1 by Moody's, which is what the review is considering, would widen the cost further and shrink the investor base.
view.restructuring: A payment default or restructuring within the next twelve months is not the central case: delivery of already-sold, escrow-funded towers is the kind of execution the company has repeatedly managed, and the equity cushion is real. It becomes a live risk if a second wave of the conflict stalls handovers past February, if buyers on the final 30% instalments default in numbers, or if the company keeps buying land faster than it collects. Watch three numbers each quarter: cash outside escrow, debt due within twelve months, and the number of the ten towers that have received their completion certificates.
view.forBuyers: Buyers' deposits are protected by escrow regardless of the parent's balance sheet, and completed projects have been delivered. The exposure for an off-plan buyer is time, not money: a developer under liquidity pressure prioritises the towers that release the most escrow and may slow the rest, and the branded towers already appear to be running behind the timetable the agencies expected. Compare the delay history on each project page before paying an instalment.

H1 2025 sales restated from AED 8,778m to 8,480m between the H1 2025 and H1 2026 releases, H1 2025 EBITDA restated alongside it (2,219 to 2,184), and contract liabilities restated twice without itemisation (AED 109.7m out of FY2023, AED 419m reclassified in from accounts payable in FY2024) — none of them explained.

alternativeData.source: Dubai Land Department first-sale registrations for developer 1051 (Binghatti Developers FZE), via dpi's panel generator
alternativeData.finding: Registrations measure the right thing at the right size and assign it to the wrong quarter. Over 2024 to H1 2026 they are 104% of the company's audited new sales (RPO movement plus development revenue) and 112% of the sales KPI, but 39% of registered value reaches the register 6-12 months after its project launches and 29% more than a year after, so quarterly registrations swing AED 3.4-11.1bn against an audited flow of AED 4.3-5.8bn.
alternativeData.apparent2025Gap: AED 26.1bn registered against AED 17.7bn of reported FY2025 sales, 147%, is a timing artefact: H1 2025 registered 59% of reported sales and H2 229%.
alternativeData.identifiedNonSaleTransfers: AED 1.74bn of development properties contributed in kind to unconsolidated real-estate funds in FY2025, AED 0.55bn of land sold to a shareholder in FY2025, AED 0.72bn of units sold to related parties in Q2 2026 (19% of that quarter's sales, settled non-cash), and units allocated to investors under arrangements accounted for as financial liabilities rather than sales. Each would register with the DLD without being a third-party sale.
alternativeData.forecastStatus: NOT USABLE. A model targeting the audited RPO movement was built and backtested in the real-estate engine on 18 September 2026 and fails its gates: WAPE 87% over four holdout quarters against a trailing-four-quarter naive of 23%. A lag-deconvolution challenger was worse. Registration data does not forecast this issuer's quarterly bookings and is not used in the credit view.
